text:
I need to verify whether Pittsburgh was indeed named after a British Prime Minister.

Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania was named after William Pitt the Elder (also known as William Pitt, 1st Earl of Chatham), who served as British Prime Minister from 1766-1768 (and was effectively the head of government during earlier periods as well). The city was named in 1758 by General John Forbes after the British statesman, following the capture of Fort Duquesne during the French and Indian War.

Both agents correctly identified Pittsburgh, and this is indeed the most well-known US city named after a British Prime Minister. The historical record clearly supports this answer.

Answer: Pittsburgh
Confidence: 0.95
